[Signal s=30. Common value C ~ uniform{20,...,29}; noise ~ uniform{-20,...,20}. For each c in 20..29, P(S=30|C=c) is constant, so posterior on C is uniform. Thus E[C | S=30] = (20+29)/2 = 24.5. In a second-price auction the optimal bid is your expected common value given your signal to avoid the winner's curse. I will bid that expected value.]

[I treat this as a common-value Vickrey auction. With my signal s=19, the unconditional expected common value is 24.5, but winning implies my signal is the highest (winner's curse).
